content:
natalie (eng-platform): Heads up — seeing intermittent gRPC streaming hangs through ALBs in eu-west-1. ~3-5% of streams start, then stop getting data mid-stream; client never sees trailers. Repro is flaky but consistent under load.
aj (eng-infra): Ugh. Any pattern on source IPs / NAT ports?
natalie (eng-platform): Initial correlation points to egress NAT port reuse spikes and conntrack nearing capacity on a subset of edge nodes. Also some long-lived streams that show zero WINDOW_UPDATE for seconds.
sam (eng-runtime): Do we have raw TCP captures? Looks like either proxy buffering or a WINDOW_UPDATE deadlock — maybe an h2 flow-control mismatch between ALB and downstream envoy.
maria (eng-sre): I pulled logs from the ingress fleet: a few entries with `http2: stream 0 stalled, no WINDOW_UPDATE` and repeated `WRITE` errors. Also seeing rise in TIME_WAIT and ephemeral port churn.
natalie (eng-platform): Example log snippet from proxy: `WARN stream stalled: id=12345 window=0 last_update=12s ago route=ai-host`
aj (eng-infra): Can you paste the envoy/http2 options we run? Might be the initial window sizes and connection window tuning.
sam (eng-runtime): Current config (excerpt):
```
http_connection_manager:
  codec_type: AUTO
  http2_protocol_options:
    initial_stream_window_size: 65536
    initial_connection_window_size: 1048576
```
sam (eng-runtime): That looks standard. If ALB terminates h2 and re-uses backend connections with different flow control semantics we can hit transient window starvation if updates are dropped at the edge.
maria (eng-sre): Also noticed a couple of ALB 504s clustered around the spike; ALB idle timeout is default 60s. Long-running, low-throughput streams might be getting clipped if keepalives aren't crossing.
natalie (eng-platform): Repro steps we used: spawn 200 parallel streaming clients that send small request then wait for server to stream tokens over ~30s. 3-5% of streams never finish. When reproducing against a direct node (bypass ALB) failure rate ~0.5%.
aj (eng-infra): So ALB+NAT+conntrack seems likely. Short-term mitigations: increase conntrack max on edge nodes, bump ip_local_port_range to avoid port exhaustion, and raise ALB idle timeout for routing groups serving long streams.
sam (eng-runtime): Runtime mitigation: add periodic WINDOW_UPDATE heartbeat from backend for idle streams (cheap keepalive frames) and reduce frame coalescing so we don't hold updates until batching.
maria (eng-sre): I'll spin a canary: bump conntrack to 200k on 10% of edge nodes and ALB idle timeout -> 300s for the affected target group. Monitor `stream_stall_rate` and `alb_504_rate`.
deploy-bot (ci): deploy started: edge/conntrack-bump -> rollout 10%
aj (eng-infra): Can we also log the per-stream last-window-update timestamp to measure gap distribution? Even a microsecond-accurate metric would help.
natalie (eng-platform): Good call. I'll add a lightweight metric: `last_window_update_ms` exported as histogram for streamed responses.
kube-bot (infra): note: increased net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range on nodes/egress-pool-3
sam (eng-runtime): Another possible fix: terminate HTTP/2 at the nearest node but proxy to backend using HTTP/1.1 for very long streams — avoids h2 flow-control interplay. Might be more invasive.
maria (eng-sre): For now we should do: 1) conntrack bump canary (done) 2) ALB idle timeout bumped for affected TGs (canary) 3) enable backend WINDOW_UPDATE heartbeat + metric 4) collect tcpdump samples for 1% of streams for 6 hours.
aj (eng-infra): I also opened an internal ticket to validate ALB behavior during connection reuse: whether it strips or coalesces WINDOW_UPDATE frames when proxying.
natalie (eng-platform): Thanks. Action items assigned: sam -> add heartbeat; maria -> rollout & tcpdump; aj -> ALB validation + port ranges; natalie -> instrument metric + coordinate with product for customer impact notices.
sam (eng-runtime): PR inbound for heartbeat and a small opt-out flag for latency-sensitive routes.
maria (eng-sre): Early canary looks promising — stream_stall_rate dropped from 4.2% to 0.8% on canary nodes after conntrack bump + ALB idle increase. Still collecting data. :thumbsup:
aj (eng-infra): Keep an eye on ephemeral port utilization cost/scale. We may need larger egress fleet if NAT hits are persistent.
natalie (eng-platform): We'll follow up tomorrow with a short postmortem and runbook for diagnosing h2 stream stalls (include ddos-like nat bursts vs flow-control bugs). Thanks all. :heart:
